quotes.stratification: Thirty male and female subjects aged 39–76 years were stratified into 5 groups based on their creatinine clearance (CLCr) values: normal renal function (NRF) (CLCr > 80 mL/min; N = 7), mild RI (50 = CLCr = 80 mL/min; N = 5), moderate RI (30 = CLCr < 50 mL/min; N = 6), severe RI (CLCr < 30 mL/min, but not on dialysis; N = 6), and end stage renal disease (ESRD, requiring dialysis; N = 6).
quotes.purpose: Results were used to refine initial dosing recommendations based on a subject’s estimated creatinine clearance.
quotes.auc_change: Compared with the pooled data from NRF and mild RI groups, mean AUC8 increased approximately 140% in moderate RI, 240% in severe RI, and 360% in ESRD (off dialysis).
quotes.mild: The mean difference in AUC8 between NRF and mild RI was < 20%.
quotes.protein_binding: Protein binding of lenalidomide was not markedly affected by RI (∼35 - 44%).
quotes.conclusion: Lenalidomide dosage adjustment should be considered for patients with CLCr < 50 mL/min.

study_abstract.quote_note: '50 = CLCr = 80' and 'AUC8' are as pasted; they are probably '≤' signs and 'AUC∞' lost in copying.

items.question: The label lists 3 healthy subjects with normal renal function in the renal study; the EMA table used as the platform's reference has n = 7 in the normal group. Are these different studies?
facts: EMA (PDF page 20): groups by 'Measured creatinine clearance (CLcr)': normal > 80 mL/min n = 7; mild 50-80 n = 5; moderate 30-<50 n = 6; severe < 30 not on dialysis n = 6; ESRD requiring dialysis n = 6; 30 subjects in all.

Label (12.3): groups by CLcr 'calculated using Cockcroft-Gault': mild 50-79 n = 8; moderate 30-49 n = 9; severe < 30 n = 4; ESRD on dialysis n = 6; healthy subjects with CLcr > 80 n = 3; 30 subjects in all.

The label's results reproduce from the EMA Table 4 group means: CL/F 207 (normal), 71 (moderate), 52 (severe), 39 mL/min (ESRD off dialysis) give decreases of 66%, 75% and 81% (label: '66% to 75%' and 'an 80% decrease'); half-lives 3.34, 10.6, 9.22 and 15.6 h give 3.2-, 2.8- and 4.7-fold increases (label: '3-fold' and 'approximate 4.5-fold').

The study abstract confirms the stratification: 30 subjects in 5 groups by creatinine clearance, N = 7, 5, 6, 6 and 6 (normal > 80, mild 50-80, moderate 30-< 50, severe < 30 not on dialysis, ESRD). It does not say how clearance was determined; its background refers to dosing 'based on a subject's estimated creatinine clearance'.

The abstract's AUC increases reproduce from the EMA Table 4 means: against the pooled normal and mild groups (mean 2425 ng.h/mL), severe +238% (abstract 'approximately 240%'), ESRD off dialysis +359% ('360%'), moderate +148% ('approximately 140%').

Label of about December 2008: 7 healthy subjects (CLcr 83-145 mL/min), and 5 mild (57-74), 6 moderate (33-46), 6 severe (17-29) and 6 ESRD patients, the same 7/5/6/6/6 as the EMA table; the 2023 label's 3/8/9/4/6 is a later regrouping of the same 30 subjects.
items.conclusion: Same study (CC-5013-PK-001, 30 subjects), classified two ways: by measured creatinine clearance in the EMA table and by Cockcroft-Gault in the label's description. The label's quantitative results correspond to the EMA's measured-clearance groups. The platform's reference (normal group, n = 7, mean AUC 2181 ng.h/mL) is unaffected. The earliest renal label (about December 2008) gives the same 7/5/6/6/6 groups as the EMA table, with each group's observed creatinine clearance range.
items.to_confirm: The full publication (Chen N, et al. J Clin Pharmacol 2007;47:1466-1475), to see whether the label's 3/8/9/4/6 grouping by Cockcroft-Gault is reported there.

items.question: Which creatinine clearance defined the renal groups used in the Hughes and Kim outside checks?
facts: The EMA table states measured creatinine clearance (PDF page 20).

The locked plans record otherwise. hughes_renal_group_check_plan_v1.json (known_differences): 'Creatinine clearance method and weight basis used to assign renal groups are not stated in the extracted pages.' kim_renal_group_check_plan_v1.json (scenario rationale): 'the study's actual method is not stated in the extracted pages'. The method statement was incorrect: the extracted page states 'Measured'. The weight basis is indeed not stated.
Both checks treated the group ranges as Cockcroft-Gault values (the models' covariate), with an assumed weight basis.

The label's Cockcroft-Gault classification of the same subjects places fewer above 80 mL/min (3 against 7) and more in 30-49 mL/min (9 against 6), so for some subjects the Cockcroft-Gault value was lower than the measured one; individual values are not available.

post_hoc_bound.method: Change in typical exposure if a group's Cockcroft-Gault value were lower than the range used in the check, from each model's covariate equation alone.
post_hoc_bound.hughes: Clearance scales as CrCl^0.224: 40 to 25 mL/min gives clearance x 0.90, exposure about 1.11-fold. Far smaller than the 2.1-fold under-prediction in the moderate group, so the method difference does not explain that result.
post_hoc_bound.kim: Clearance scales as exp(0.0131 x eGFR): 5, 10 and 15 mL/min lower gives exposure about 1.07-, 1.14- and 1.22-fold (treating a change in Cockcroft-Gault clearance as an equal change in eGFR, an approximation). Comparable to Kim's 1.3-fold under-prediction in the severe group, so Kim's severe and moderate results may be sensitive to the method difference.

items.conclusion: The locked results stand as recorded. The plans' statement about the clearance method is corrected here. The difference cannot explain the Hughes moderate-group result, but it could account for part of Kim's severe-group under-prediction. The scope band edges (50 and 30 mL/min) come from the measured-clearance groups and are applied to each model's estimated clearance; this is recorded, and the scope files are unchanged.

items.question: The label's first renal dose step is CLcr 30 to 60 mL/min; the platform's reference note (from Chen 2017, a secondary source) describes dose reductions below 50 mL/min. Which figure does the platform use?
facts: No platform calculation uses a dose threshold. The 50 mL/min figures in the scopes, band notes and special-population summaries are the EMA study's moderate-group boundary (measured clearance, 30 to < 50), not a dose threshold.
The only dose-threshold statement is the reference note's quotation of Chen 2017, already marked as a secondary summary.
The label is quoted as it stands (lenalidomide_label_2023_v1.json, Table 3).

The study's own conclusion was 'Lenalidomide dosage adjustment should be considered for patients with CLCr < 50 mL/min', with recommended myeloma starting doses of 10 mg daily (moderate), 15 mg every 48 h (severe) and 15 mg three times a week after dialysis (ESRD).
The current label (revision 3/2023) starts dose reduction at CLcr 60 mL/min and gives 5 mg daily, after dialysis on dialysis days, for patients requiring dialysis.

June 2006 myeloma label (supplement 001): no renal dose table; 'No formal studies have been conducted in patients with renal impairment', and patients with renal insufficiency were excluded from the trials.

First renal table found, label of about December 2008 (supplements 006/016/017): myeloma moderate impairment '30 ≤ CLcr < 60' (Cockcroft-Gault), 10 mg every 24 hours; the text above says adjustment is recommended for CLcr < 60 mL/min.

February 2015 label (supplement 041): a separate myeloma table starting at CLcr 30-50 mL/min, while the MDS and MCL table and the text above both tables say < 60, so the label is internally inconsistent for myeloma.
February 2017 label (supplement 049, maintenance approval) and every later label held: one table starting at CLcr 30 to 60 mL/min for all indications.
items.conclusion: 60 mL/min was the label's myeloma threshold from the first renal table (about December 2008), although the renal study's abstract recommended < 50. The February 2015 label's myeloma table at 30-50 is the exception, inconsistent with its own text, and the February 2017 label restored 30-60. Whether labels between 2009 and 2015 used 50 or 60, and why the label departed from the study's recommendation, are not established from the files held.
items.to_confirm: The review for the supplement that first added renal dosing (about 2008), which should explain the 60 mL/min threshold; optionally labels between 2009 and 2015.

items.question: The study abstract says the mean difference in AUC between normal function and mild impairment was below 20%; the EMA Table 4 means differ by 27%. Which is right?
facts: EMA Table 4 (PDF page 21): mean AUC to infinity 2181 (normal, n = 7) and 2767 ng.h/mL (mild, n = 5); ratio 1.27.
Abstract: 'The mean difference in AUC8 between NRF and mild RI was < 20%.'
items.conclusion: Not reconciled. The abstract may use another statistic (for example geometric means or least-squares means) that it does not name. The platform uses the EMA arithmetic means, as recorded in renal_pk_group_evidence_v1.json; the Hughes and Kim checks classified the mild group as consistent either way.

items.question: Protein binding: the label says approximately 30%; the abstract reports about 35-44% across renal groups.
facts: Label 12.3: 'In vitro [14C]-lenalidomide binding to plasma proteins is approximately 30%.'
Abstract: '∼35 - 44%' in the study subjects.
The EMA assessment reports 23% and 29% in plasma from myeloma patients and healthy volunteers (PDF page 20); Kim 2026 estimated an unbound fraction of 0.614 (binding about 39%).
items.conclusion: Recorded. Sources differ in method and population (in vitro versus subjects). No platform calculation uses a binding value except Kim's own estimated unbound fraction.

items.question: Who were the subjects of the renal study CC-5013-PK-001? The platform's EMA extract records their disease context as 'not established'.
facts: Label of about December 2008: 'The pharmacokinetics of lenalidomide were studied in patients with renal impairment due to nonmalignant conditions', with 7 healthy subjects of similar age as controls.
February 2015 label, section 2.4: the dose adjustment is 'based on a pharmacokinetic study in patients with renal impairment due to non-malignant conditions'.
The 2017 and 2023 labels no longer contain this phrase.

source.quote: In this study, 5 patients with mild renal function impairment (creatinine clearance 57-74 mL/min), 6 patients with moderate renal function impairment (creatinine clearance 33-46 mL/min), 6 patients with severe renal function impairment (creatinine clearance 17-29 mL/min), and 6 patients with end stage renal disease requiring dialysis were administered a single oral 25-mg dose of REVLIMID® (lenalidomide).
source.location: Clinical Pharmacology, Special Populations, PDF page 6

items.conclusion: The renal study enrolled people whose renal impairment was due to non-malignant conditions, not myeloma patients. The pinned EMA extract (renal_pk_group_evidence_v1.json) and the Hughes scope's disease rule still say the outside study's disease context is not established; those files are not changed here. The study should be read as a non-cancer population when compared with the myeloma-based models; this is one possible contributor to model-versus-study differences, not tested.

items.question: What creatinine clearance did each renal study group actually have?
facts: Label of about December 2008: normal 83-145, mild 57-74, moderate 33-46, severe 17-29 mL/min (method not named in that sentence; the label's dose table uses Cockcroft-Gault).

The Hughes and Kim checks sampled creatinine clearance across the group definitions (normal 80-140 or wider, mild 50-80, moderate 30-50, severe 10-30, 5-30 or 20-30 depending on scenario), not these observed ranges; each observed range lies inside the corresponding sampled interval.
items.conclusion: Recorded for any future check. The observed moderate range (33-46) partly lies below the Hughes model's data (36 mL/min) and the severe range (17-29) wholly below it. Because the observed ranges sit inside the intervals the checks sampled, using them is unlikely to reverse the recorded results, but a recheck would need a new locked plan; the existing results stand.
